data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The count is 648, derived by modeling the lexical order generation of digit strings via a Dirichlet energy landscape where the hundreds digit has an infinite barrier at zero, and the tens and units digits experience harmonic exclusion potentials, resulting in exactly 9\u00d79\u00d78 admissible stable states.","counterconditions":[{"case":"This model fails if the formal problem allows leading zeros (which would alter the ground state count to 10\u00d79\u00d78 = 720).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The energy landscape analogy collapses if the digits are not independent sites with symmetric exclusion, but instead undergo quantum entanglement.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"We model the construction of a three-digit number as finding a ground state in a 1D lattice of 3 sites (H, T, U). The Hamiltonian assigns infinite energy if H=0. It adds a pairwise penalty V=\u221e if any two sites share the same digit value. The partition function over this discrete configuration space exactly factors: the domain of H has 9 states; T has 10 minus 1 excluded state (H); U has 10 minus 2 excluded states (H, T). The partition function evaluates to 9\u00d79\u00d78 = 648.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
